issue.title: ArduCopter – fly_mission.cpp example
issue.body:
Hi,
I tried running the fly_mission.cpp when connecting to SITL – ArduCopter.
I get the following indications:
  Uploading mission…
  Falling back to gimbal protocol v1 (mission_impl.cpp:128)
  Invalid sequence for ArduPilot items (mavlink_mission_transfer.cpp:249)
  Mission upload failed: Error, exiting.

Do you know why is that?
After reading some of the forums – I think this might be because for ArduCopter, I must set the home_location as the first mission_item. Is that the reason?
And if so – what would be a correct way to implement this in C++?
Thanks.

comments.body:
> Is that the reason?

I am not entirely sure of the root cause, but the error you see is triggered here: https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/main/src/mavsdk/core/mavlink_mission_transfer.cpp#L249. I don't know if this ever worked.

I know that the `mission_raw` should work, but I don't think the `mission` plugin ever did. And intuitively I would think that `mavlink_mission_transfer` is used for both, so it _should_ work. However, maybe the `mission` plugin is not sending a valid list of items for Ardupilot.

Would you like to debug this?

For a quick test, you could try e.g. e.g. [in mission_impl.cpp](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/main/src/mavsdk/plugins/mission/mission_impl.cpp) to test if it is `Ardupilot`:

```cpp
if (_system_impl->autopilot() == SystemImpl::Autopilot::ArduPilot)
```

And if it is, add some home position as a first waypoint.

> However, maybe the mission plugin is not sending a valid list of items for Ardupilot.

I think that's right.

Hi @ygratz, for reference on how to create a valid mission for Ardupilot, please have a look at the integration test:

https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/2caa1c57c8ab2cfaf82fe4c976c991f0c691f28d/src/integration_tests/mission_raw_import_and_fly.cpp#L90

and

https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/2caa1c57c8ab2cfaf82fe4c976c991f0c691f28d/src/integration_tests/mission_raw_import_and_fly.cpp#L151

I just posted in #728 with the same issue. Perhaps I have shed some light on the problem and the expected ArduPilot format now? 

I definitely could be wrong, but I think the ```MissionRaw::MissionItem``` does not contain the correct arguments...
I was wrong. The sequence just increases normally from 0, even if 0 is the home position.

issue.title: corrected mission item seq check for ardupilot

repository.name: MAVSDK
repository.description: API and library for MAVLink compatible systems written in C++ 20

issue.body:
This PR corrects the mission item sequence check for ardupilot. 

Solves https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/issues/728 and https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/issues/2023


ArduPilot Mission Plan sequence starts at 0 just like PX4. Its just that the item 0 should be home position and item 1 should be takeoff and then follows other mission items. In this PR, the special check for Ardupilot is removed since the same check which is used for PX4 should work for ardupilot as well.

timeline.body: I was wrong. The sequence just increases normally from 0, even if 0 is the home position.

issue.title: Adding support for ArduPilot

repository.name: MAVSDK
repository.description: API and library for MAVLink compatible systems written in C++ 20

issue.body:
## Context

A while ago, @peterbarker worked on adding support for APM in the SDK ([here](https://github.com/peterbarker/DroneCore/tree/ardupilot)). More recently, @jinchengde (and others) started looking into that, again. The goal of this issue is to discuss the high-level requirements and architecture.

## Benefits for APM

The project is architectured in such a way that everything relies on a C++ MAVLink implementation. Making this implementation compatible with APM means that APM will also get the language bindings ([Python](https://github.com/dronecode/dronecodesdk-python), [Swift](https://github.com/dronecode/dronecodesdk-swift), [Java](https://github.com/dronecore/dronecore-java) and future ones like [Javascript](https://github.com/mrpollo/DronecodeSDK-JavaScript)).

The interface common to all our bindings is defined [here](https://github.com/Dronecode/DronecodeSDK-Proto/tree/master/protos) and is used to auto-generate language-specific APIs (e.g. using RxSwift in Swift, RxJava in Java, and asyncio in Python).

## SDK architecture (overview)

The SDK can been seen as composed from 4 parts:

1. The [interface definition](https://github.com/Dronecode/DronecodeSDK-Proto/tree/master/protos) (protobuf files), common to all the languages (C++, Swift, Java, Python). Each proto file is considered a "plugin", which is a group of (MAVLink) features.
2. The C++ [MAVLink implementation](https://github.com/Dronecode/DronecodeSDK), which actually maintains a connection to the drone and does the MAVLink logic.
3. The [backend](https://github.com/Dronecode/DronecodeSDK/tree/develop/backend), which exposes the C++ implementation of (2) as a messaging server through the interface of (1).
4. The language bindings ([Python](https://github.com/dronecode/dronecodesdk-python), [Swift](https://github.com/dronecode/dronecodesdk-swift), [Java](https://github.com/dronecore/dronecore-java)), which implement (1) to communicate with the backend (3).

At the lowest level, each plugin (defined by one proto file) is a C++ library. The backend uses those libraries, as can been seen [here](https://github.com/Dronecode/DronecodeSDK/blob/develop/backend/src/CMakeLists.txt#L38-L46).
